newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs may consolidate more, undertone good.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs may consolidate more, undertone good.

text.p: Belgian OLOs looked likely to spend another quiet day in consolidation mode on Tuesday, but the outlook for the next few weeks was positive, dealers said.
"Of course it depends on how Bunds close -- and there was little activity today in Belgium -- but the medium trend is up, and the mood is still okay," one said.

Confidence has been bolstered after weaker U.S. jobs data on Friday which lessened expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise U.S. short-term rates at the next FOMC policy meeting in mid-November. U.S. Treasuries succumbed to slight profit-taking on Monday after rallying on the data the previous session.
"We could spend the week consolidating but the major uptrend is intact," another said.

The benchmark 2006 OLO finished with a yield of 6.11 percent, up from 6.08 percent at the close on Friday. However prices held up slightly better than German bonds, with the yield spread over Bunds narrowing two basis points to 10 bp.

One dealer said the spread should stay in a 10 to 15 basis point range in the coming weeks. Others thought it could return once more to single figures after touching a record eight basis points on Friday.
December bond futures slipped 17 bp to 119.21 points.
In the money markets T-bills ended quoting 3.01/05 percent, barely moved from Friday's levels.
The Belgian franc held little changed to the mark, ending at 20.5920/30.
